text: If all partial derivatives of f: ℝⁿ → ℝ exist at a point p, then f is necessarily differentiable (has a total derivative) at p.
explanation: False. The book warns that a function can possess all partial derivatives at a point yet fail to be differentiable there, because the partials probe only the coordinate directions while differentiability demands the linear approximation f(p+h) = f(p) + Df(p)h + o(|h|) to hold from every direction. Continuity of the partial derivatives near p is a sufficient extra condition that does guarantee differentiability.
